*   New [`-P`](link_4) command line option and [`PYTHONSAFEPATH`](link_4) environment variable to [disable automatically prepending potentially unsafe paths](https://docs.python.org/3.11/whatsnew/3.11.html#whatsnew311-pythonsafepath) to [`sys.path`](link_5)

This feature requires storing column positions in [Code Objects](link_11), which may result in a small increase in interpreter memory usage and disk usage for compiled Python files. To avoid storing the extra information and deactivate printing the extra traceback information, use the [`-X no_debug_ranges`](link_4) command line option or the [`PYTHONNODEBUGRANGES`](link_4) environment variable.

*   Added a [`-P`](link_4) command line option and a [`PYTHONSAFEPATH`](link_4) environment variable, which disable the automatic prepending to [`sys.path`](link_5) of the script’s directory when running a script, or the current directory when using [`-c`](link_4) and [`-m`](link_4). This ensures only stdlib and installed modules are picked up by [`import`](link_38), and avoids unintentionally or maliciously shadowing modules with those in a local (and typically user-writable) directory. (Contributed by Victor Stinner in [gh-57684](link_39).)

*   Bytes are no longer accepted on [`sys.path`](link_5). Support broke sometime between Python 3.2 and 3.6, with no one noticing until after Python 3.10.0 was released. In addition, bringing back support would be problematic due to interactions between [`-b`](link_4) and [`sys.path_importer_cache`](link_5) when there is a mixture of [`str`](link_31) and [`bytes`](link_31) keys. (Contributed by Thomas Grainger in [gh-91181](link_43).)
